title: Frailty, thy name is marriage
html_source:
Hamlet says, “Frailty, thy name is woman! /
A little month, or ere those shoes were old / With which she follow’d my poor father’s body.” By woman, he refers to Gertrude, who is morally weak, because she has betrayed her husband by marrying his brother, Claudius just after a month of her husband’s death.
